doc.title: Ray Shiner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 1998

title: Recording sessions and the kazoo tune Sunshine Girl
summary: Sight-reading in studio, Finegan refusing another take, and the kazoo novelty.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: When you went in to do a recording session, how long did you usually get in the studio to do a record?
Usually, I don’t know, you were supposed to do three or four numbers in three hours. Sometimes we’d do five or six and we’d be sight reading.

There was one number we did, the A & R man came on and he says, “Okay, let’s do another one.” Finegan says, “No, we’re not doing another one.” He says, “Why not?” He says, “The guys in the band don’t want to do another one, they like that one.” He says, “There’s a couple of mistakes.” Finegan says, “The hell with the mistakes, the feel was there.” And of course we had our revenge. RCA wanted us to do something with kazoos because that was the rage. So Finegan, something that Bob Merrill wrote, he’s the guy that wrote “Take Me Along” for Jackie Gleason, because he was a pop composer. So Finegan wrote “Sunshine Girl,” which was the name of the tune, for 21 kazoos, with jazz kazoo, played by Sonny Russo and Nick Travis.
Oh we recorded it. One of the biggest hits we ever made. Strictly a put on, right? I could tell you stories about that band.
